# .github/ — CI standard and release lane

The job table, then the rules for editing anything here.

## Jobs

GitHub Actions on GitHub-hosted runners — `ubuntu-latest` default (`ubuntu-24.04-arm` for arm64). `test` runs against `docker-compose.dev.yml` (state + target Postgres, MySQL, Mongo, Redis, Dragonfly) — the stack `bin/test` uses locally — started in the background so its boot overlaps the compile. Rust jobs install the toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` pins with the runner's `rustup` (no `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`); jobs with a rust-cache uninstall the runner's `stable`, because rust-cache keys on every installed toolchain. `bin/ci` reproduces `ci.yml` locally.

| Job | Does |
|---|---|
| `fmt` | `cargo fmt --check`; every action pinned to a 40-hex SHA |
| `changes` | path filters over raw NUL-delimited paths emit `code` (docs-only PRs — `website/**`, `docs/**`, `.claude/**`, `*.md`, never `.dz/**` — skip the Rust jobs; a `main` push always runs them, since `build` publishes that commit), `deps` (lock, manifests, audit config), `image` (Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, Cargo, `src/`, migrations, `third_party/`, `config/example.yaml`; PRs only), `msrv` (manifests, lock, `build.rs`, `src/`, `third_party/`), `website` (`website/`, `README.md`; PRs only), `deploy` (`deploy/`, `src/startup/metrics/catalogue.rs`, `bin/check-deploy`, `ci.yml`; every `main` push). A job skips only on an explicit `false`, so a failed `changes` runs them all. A PR diffs `HEAD^1..HEAD` (the merge commit); a push diffs `github.event.before..HEAD`, and an all-zero or unfetchable `before` sets every output true |
| `clippy` | `clippy -D warnings` twice on one `--profile ci` graph: `--all-targets`, then lib + bins with `-C debug-assertions=off` (the shipping cfg); plus `bin/check-scrub-features` |
| `test` | `cargo nextest run --profile ci --cargo-profile ci --all-targets --all-features` (`--no-run` first, then after the dev stack is healthy) minus `deploy_catalogue::promtool_accepts_the_rules` (the `deploy` job's); JUnit uploaded (`.config/nextest.toml`) |
| `deploy` | `bin/check-deploy` when `deploy` is true: `promtool check rules`, `helm lint --strict` (chart + `ci/full-values.yaml`), kubeconform `-strict` on the rendered chart and kustomize base (CRD schemas from `datreeio/CRDs-catalog` at a pinned commit); every tool a digest-pinned image, no Rust |
| `yugabyte` | `bin/test-yugabyte` against `yugabytedb/yugabyte:2.25.2.0-b359` (the version a production deployment runs; compose profile `yugabyte`, YSQL on 5435); the Postgres query-path `it_db` modules listed in nextest's `yugabyte` profile (a new module is absent until added there), minus the NOTIFY tests YB ignores |
| `audit` | `cargo audit` (`cargo-audit` pinned) — only when `deps` changed (H8: an advisory blocks only the PR that can fix it) |
| `secret-scan` | must succeed on every run: `gate` (`ci_gate.py`) has no skip for it, and `merge` publishes only behind `gate` — `bin/secret-scan` over the index — contents, file names and symlink targets, shared with `.githooks/pre-commit --staged` — for `dbmcp_svc_[0-9a-f]{64}`, a hit reported as `path:line` only (the log is public; a token in a path is masked); exempt paths: `tests/**`, `website/**`, `config/example.yaml`, `.github/**`, `src/config/yaml/**` |
| `public-tree` | `python3 -I .github/scripts/public_tree.py` on every PR, docs-only included (no `changes` gate): no internal host, private repo, private CI provider, setup-mode name or home path in any tracked file; rules pinned by `test_public_tree.py` |
| `scripts` | every `tests/bin/*.test.sh` and every `.github/scripts/test_*.py` |
| `image-check` | PRs where `image` is true: Dockerfile build, amd64, no push, reads `main`'s gha cache |
| `msrv` | `cargo +<rust-version from Cargo.toml> check --locked` when `msrv` is true |
| `website` | `npm ci`, typecheck, build when `website` is true |
| `gate` | `if: always()`, needs every quality job; green only on success or a skip `changes` ordered (`.github/scripts/ci_gate.py`). The single required check |
| `build` + `merge` | on `main`: per-arch image (BuildKit SBOM + max-mode provenance, `GIT_SHA` build arg) → multi-arch manifest, pushed to GHCR **and** DOCR. `merge` (stages each registry's index under `index-<7>`, cosign-signs it keyless and attests its provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, and only then writes `sha-<7>` + `main` onto that digest) needs `build`, `gate` and every quality job, and runs only when `build` and `gate` succeeded. `tests/` is out of the Docker context (`.dockerignore` is an allowlist) |
| `audit` (`audit.yml`) | daily `cargo audit` on `main`; a failure opens or updates the issue the workflow owns (opened by `github-actions[bot]`, carrying a hidden body marker — never matched by title), a clean run closes it. The issue-writing job runs on `refs/heads/main` only, and only while the audited SHA is still `main`'s tip (a re-run of an older run never touches the issue) |
| `weekly` (`weekly.yml`) | Mondays, advisory: `cargo update --dry-run` report, `image-scan` (trivy, pinned by digest, on GHCR `:latest`, `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` each; HIGH/CRITICAL with a fix fails the run) and `coverage` (`cargo llvm-cov nextest` against the dev stack; a report, no threshold) |
| `load-gate` (`load-gate.yml`) | Mondays: three runners each run the benchmark harness; `verdict` fails only when two of the three regressed against the stored baseline (a missing result counts as regressed); `measure` legs are `continue-on-error`, so one dead leg never fails the run by itself |
| `codeql` (`codeql.yml`) | advisory: CodeQL `rust` (build-mode none) on `main` pushes, PRs touching Rust sources or manifests, and weekly; findings in the Security tab, not in `gate` |
| `release` (`release.yml`) | on `v*`: `preflight` (tag is an ancestor of `origin/main`, matches Cargo.toml, moving tags only move forward) → `reuse` waits for `ci.yml`'s push run on the tagged commit and probes `sha-<7>` in **both** registries → `merge` re-tags that manifest (per-arch digests = the tested ones; release version/revision/source as index annotations): version tags in both registries first, then cosign keyless signature + provenance attestation, `:latest` in both last → `chart` (after `merge`, `.github/scripts/publish_chart.sh`): the Helm chart at the release version to `ghcr.io/developerz-ai/charts/db-mcp-gateway` (its own path, GHCR only), signed and attested; `github_release` waits for it, and a re-run reuses a chart the commit already pushed. Red CI, no CI run or a missing image blocks the release — there is no build-from-the-tag fallback |
| `workflow-lint` (`workflow-lint.yml`) | advisory — actionlint (pinned image digest) + the hook tests (`python3 -I .claude/hooks/test_hooks.py`) on PRs and `main` pushes touching `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/scripts/**` or `.claude/hooks/**` |
| `release-smoke` (`release-smoke.yml`) | advisory, post-publish — after each successful `release`, Tuesdays on the Latest release, and by hand: pulls the published image per arch (amd64 + arm64) **and** per registry (GHCR anonymously, DOCR with `DOCR_TOKEN`; PR runs smoke GHCR only), checks its platform and that `--version` reports the tag, boots it against a throwaway state DB (`/healthz` 200, unauthenticated `/mcp` 401), and on the scheduled run that `:latest` is the Latest release |

`timeout-minutes` is ~2× measured p95 (clippy 15, test 20, small jobs 5, CI image build 30; the release per-arch build 60 for a cold compile). `ci.yml` cancels superseded **PR** runs only — `main` pushes get a per-SHA group and never cancel, because the Image Updater pins the short SHA and a cancelled run would leave that commit with no image (`main` is a moving convenience tag).

## Rules

- **The gate.** What blocks a merge is whatever GitHub enforces live, and that is the only authority: the rulesets (`gh api repos/developerz-ai/db-mcp-gateway/rulesets`, then each by id) **and** classic branch protection (`gh api repos/developerz-ai/db-mcp-gateway/branches/main/protection`), which still exists until the owner retires it. Never re-declare the required-check list as fact in a doc; `.dz/maintainer/maintainer.yml` names it only so the agent knows whose red check it is. `ci.yml`'s `gate` job is built to be the single required check; the decision is `.github/scripts/ci_gate.py`.
- **Skipped means passed.** GitHub counts a skipped required job as passing. `ci.yml`'s path filters rely on that: `changes` emits `code`/`deps`/`image`/`msrv`/`website`, and a filtered job skips only on an explicit `false` (a failed `changes` runs them all). `gate` re-checks every skip against `changes`' outputs, and `ci_gate.py`'s table must name every job in `gate.needs` (the gate fails red otherwise). A job-level `if:` is still a decision, not a convenience: a new skip condition is a merge that ran nothing.
- **Runners.** GitHub-hosted only (public repo): `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm` for native arm64. No self-hosted runners, so a fork PR never reaches persistent hardware.
- **Pins.** Every `uses:` is a 40-hex SHA with the version in a trailing comment; `ci.yml`'s `fmt` job and `bin/ci` (so `bin/check`) both fail an unpinned ref under `.github/workflows/`. Tools installed by `taiki-e/install-action` carry an exact version (`cargo-audit@…`, `cargo-nextest@…`). Copy a pin already used in another workflow before adding a new one; Dependabot keeps them fresh (`dependabot.yml`, 14-day cooldown). Docker images run by a step are pinned by digest.
- **Least privilege.** Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; a job that needs more asks for it itself. `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout.
- **Concurrency and timeouts.** Every workflow declares a `concurrency` group and every job sets `timeout-minutes`. `ci.yml` cancels superseded PR runs, and its `main` pushes get a per-SHA group so they never cancel; `release.yml`, `pages.yml`, `weekly.yml`, `load-gate.yml`, `audit.yml` and `release-smoke.yml` never cancel, on any event.
- **Caches.** Saved from `main` only (pushes and `ci.yml`'s Monday warm run); PRs restore. Rust keys carry the ISO week; `test` and `yugabyte` share one key that only `test` saves; until the new week's entry exists, `yugabyte` (always) and `test` (off `main`) look it up through the Actions cache API (`actions: read`) and restore last week's instead of compiling cold. Node's `~/.npm` is saved by `pages.yml` on `main` and restored by `ci.yml`'s `website` job.
- **The release tag is the input.** `release.yml` fires on a `v*` tag pushed onto the merge commit of a `chore(release)` PR, checks it is on `main` and against `Cargo.toml`, waits for `ci.yml`'s push run on that commit and re-tags its tested `sha-<7>` manifest (red CI, no CI run or a missing image in either registry blocks the release — nothing untested ships), signs it, and cuts the GitHub Release. A published tag is never moved or deleted; a broken release ships as the next patch (`.dz/schedules/release-due.md`). `release-smoke.yml` then pulls what was published and checks it runs.
- **Lint workflows before pushing.** `workflow-lint.yml` runs actionlint on every change here. Locally: `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7 -no-color`.
- **Secrets.** Two secrets: `DOCR_TOKEN` in the jobs that touch DOCR (`ci.yml` `build`/`merge`, `release.yml` `reuse`/`merge`, `release-smoke.yml`'s DOCR leg — never on a PR run), and `PUBLIC_TREE_PRIVATE_WORDS` in `ci.yml`'s `public-tree` job. Keyless signing needs no secret: `merge` (and `release.yml`'s `chart`) asks for `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` itself. Beyond them, the run's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` logs in to GHCR in the push jobs and files the advisory issue in `audit.yml` (`issues: write`, its `issue` job alone, on `main` alone). A new secret is read in the one job that needs it, never at workflow level.
